title: UX theming layer priorities and component fallbacks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a deterministic layering model for theme tokens and a fallback/override policy to ensure consistent visuals across brand themes (customer brand accents), dark mode, and high-contrast variants. Scope: tokens for buttons, tables, charts, icons; component-level overrides; chart palette harmonization; accessible contrast targets; runtime considerations for theme swap.
Problem: Multiple independent token sources (core system, brand accents, surface adjustments, user prefs) are producing inconsistent results in dark mode—button focus rings sometimes fail contrast targets, chart series colors clash with surfaces, and table zebra stripes lose hierarchy when density is compact.
Proposal summary: 1) Introduce a three-tier token precedence model (Core -> Surface Adjustments -> Brand Accents) with explicit Conflict Resolution Rules. 2) Add 'fusion tokens' as computed tokens that blend Core and Brand values using contrast-preserving transforms for dark mode. 3) Component-level override contract: each component can opt into fusion token usage or explicit override keys. 4) Chart palette harmonizer: algorithmic palette generator that produces accessible palettes by deriving from brand accent and testing against surface luminance. 5) Button and table state token audit and targeted fixes for focus/hover/disabled states.
acceptance_criteria: Layer precedence documented and diagrammed in Confluence with examples for common conflicts (button background vs brand accent)
Fusion token transforms implemented in design token generator and validated in Figma token library
Button states (default/hover/active/focus/disabled) meet WCAG AA contrast ratios against both surface and elevated cards in dark mode
Chart palette generator produces >=5 distinct series colors per brand that pass contrast checks against chart backgrounds and labels
Table row/zebra and divider tokens maintain perceived hierarchy at compact densities and in high-contrast theme
Console build includes runtime flags to toggle fusion tokens per-tenant and a feature flag for gradual rollout
comments: 2026-03-04 Maya Patel: Initial design spike completed. Created layer precedence diagram; uploaded to Confluence. Recommend 'fusion token' approach to avoid hard brand overrides on functional tokens.

2026-03-06 Liam O'Connor (ENG): Reviewed spike—concern about runtime cost of blending transforms on the fly. Suggested precomputing two sets (light/dark) during token build pipeline. Action: ENG to prototype precompute (ENG-51234).
2026-03-08 Sofia Martinez (PM): Prioritize chart palette harmonization for next release due to customer complaints around unreadable charts in dark mode. Adjusted scope and estimate.
2026-03-10 Ava Chen: Figma library updated with fusion token examples for buttons and table rows. Requested visual QA steps and test permutations for compact/comfortable densities.

2026-03-12 Design review: Decided to require component opt-in for fusion tokens; global overrides disallowed unless explicit migration path. Agreed to use Chromatic + Percy for visual diffs. Assigned ENG-51800 to implement token-generator changes.
notes: Trade-offs: Fusion tokens increase token set complexity but reduce ad-hoc overrides in components. Precomputing mitigates runtime overhead but increases build artifacts.
Edge cases: Third-party charting library color clashes; plan to provide adapter utility that maps generated palette to library palette indices.
Rollout: Phased — internal consoles first, then beta customers, then general availability behind release console-2026.04 flag.
